description: Graduate treatment of wireless communication from channel physics to 5G, massive MIMO, mobility, IoT and satellite links. Students derive link budgets and capacity results, simulate fading and multi-cell networks, and design coverage for rural African settings.
modelledOn: Tse and Viswanath, Fundamentals of Wireless Communication
Dahlman, Parkvall and Skold, 5G NR: The Next Generation Wireless Access Technology
outcomes: Compute link budgets and apply path-loss, shadowing and fading models to predict coverage and outage.
Derive and simulate bit error rate, capacity and diversity gain for modulation, coding and OFDM links in fading channels.
Analyse random-access and scheduling protocols for throughput, delay and fairness under contention.
Explain 5G architecture and evaluate multi-antenna precoding, beamforming and handover performance in a multi-cell simulation.
Design and evaluate a rural coverage, IoT or satellite network against energy, capacity and cost constraints.

units.title: Wireless channel models and fading
topics: Link budget: free-space, log-distance and two-ray path loss, Friis equation and shadowing
Large-scale models: Okumura-Hata and COST-231 for urban and rural cells in Africa
Small-scale fading: Rayleigh and Rician, Doppler spread, coherence time and coherence bandwidth
Multipath, delay spread and intersymbol interference; the tapped delay line model
Capacity: Shannon, ergodic and outage capacity in fading channels
Diversity: selection, maximal ratio combining, Alamouti coding and diversity order

units.title: Modulation, coding and OFDM
topics: Bit error rate of BPSK, QPSK and M-QAM in AWGN and in Rayleigh fading
Channel coding: convolutional, turbo, LDPC and polar codes; coding gain
OFDM: cyclic prefix, subcarrier orthogonality and peak-to-average power ratio; SC-FDMA
Link adaptation: adaptive modulation and coding and hybrid ARQ
Channel estimation with pilots and frequency-domain equalisation

units.title: MAC protocols and spectrum access
topics: ALOHA, slotted ALOHA and CSMA/CA throughput; hidden and exposed terminals
IEEE 802.11 DCF and the Bianchi saturation model; 802.11ax OFDMA
Scheduling: round robin, max C/I and proportional fair
Cognitive radio and dynamic spectrum access; TV white space
Spectrum policy: licensed, unlicensed and shared bands in Africa

units.title: Cellular architecture, 5G and beyond
topics: Cell structure: frequency reuse, SINR, sectorisation and interference
LTE evolved packet core and the 5G core service-based architecture
5G NR physical layer: numerology, frame structure and bandwidth parts
5G use cases: eMBB, URLLC, mMTC and network slicing
Open RAN, small cells and heterogeneous networks
Rural coverage and fixed wireless access economics
Beyond 5G: reconfigurable surfaces, terahertz bands and integrated sensing and communication

units.title: Massive MIMO and beamforming
topics: MIMO channel model, spatial multiplexing and SVD-based capacity
Precoding: zero-forcing, MMSE and multi-user MIMO
Massive MIMO: channel hardening, pilot contamination and TDD reciprocity
Beamforming: array factor, beam steering and millimetre-wave beam management
Hybrid analogue-digital beamforming

units.title: Mobility management and handover
topics: Mobility models: random waypoint and Gauss-Markov
Handover: hysteresis, time-to-trigger, the A3 event and ping-pong effects
Location management: tracking areas and paging
Mobile IP and mobility anchoring in the 5G core
Handover failure analysis for high-speed vehicles and trains

units.title: Wireless sensor and IoT networks
topics: Low-power wide-area networks: LoRa spreading factors, duty cycle limits, LoRaWAN and NB-IoT
Short-range links: Bluetooth Low Energy, IEEE 802.15.4, Zigbee and 6LoWPAN
Energy models, duty cycling and sensor MAC protocols: S-MAC and B-MAC
Routing in sensor networks: RPL, LEACH and directed diffusion
Energy harvesting and precision-agriculture deployment design
Localisation and time synchronisation: RSSI, time of arrival and trilateration

units.title: Satellite and non-terrestrial links
topics: Orbits: GEO, MEO and LEO; Kepler's laws, visibility windows and Doppler
Satellite link budget: EIRP, G/T and rain fade
LEO constellations: handover between satellites, inter-satellite links and latency
Satellite access: DVB-S2, VSAT and MF-TDMA; TCP over satellite paths
High-altitude platforms, drones and non-terrestrial networks in 5G
Connecting remote communities: satellite versus terrestrial options

units.title: Research methods and project
topics: Reading wireless research: channel measurement and testbed papers
Simulation methodology: Monte Carlo of fading channels and confidence intervals
Project: design and evaluate a rural coverage or IoT network
Open problems: spectrum scarcity, energy efficiency and wireless security

schedule.title: Path loss and propagation models
schedule.exercise: Compute the link budget and coverage radius of a 900 MHz rural cell in northern Ghana using two empirical models and compare the answers.

tasks.title: Compute free-space and log-distance path loss at five distances and find the maximum range for a given transmit power and receiver sensitivity
Apply the Okumura-Hata model for urban, suburban and rural areas at 900 MHz and plot received power against distance for each
Simulate Rayleigh fading with Doppler spread, measure level crossing rate and fade duration, and compare them with theory

schedule.title: Multipath, capacity and diversity
schedule.exercise: Derive the outage capacity of a Rayleigh channel and show by simulation how diversity combining steepens the error curve.

tasks.title: Convolve a transmitted pulse train with a three-tap multipath channel and identify where intersymbol interference corrupts the symbols
Estimate ergodic and 10 percent outage capacity of a Rayleigh channel by Monte Carlo and compare with the Shannon capacity at average SNR
Simulate BPSK with selection, maximal ratio combining and Alamouti coding, and fit the diversity order from the slope of each BER curve

schedule.title: Modulation, coding and OFDM
schedule.exercise: Build an OFDM link with a cyclic prefix and link adaptation, and plot its throughput against SNR in a multipath channel.

tasks.title: Plot the theoretical bit error rate of BPSK, QPSK and 16-QAM against SNR in AWGN and read off the SNR needed for a BER of 0.001
Implement an OFDM transmitter and receiver with a cyclic prefix and show it removes intersymbol interference in a two-tap channel
Design an adaptive modulation and coding table with SNR thresholds that maximises throughput at a block error rate target of 10 percent

schedule.title: Random access, scheduling and spectrum
schedule.exercise: Evaluate the throughput of slotted ALOHA and CSMA/CA, then compare schedulers for users with different channel qualities.

tasks.title: Plot the throughput of ALOHA and slotted ALOHA against offered load and mark the maximum value of each
Simulate round robin, max C/I and proportional fair scheduling for ten users and compare total throughput and Jain fairness
Simulate 802.11 contention with 5 to 50 stations and compare the measured saturation throughput with the Bianchi model prediction

schedule.title: Cellular structure and the 5G system
schedule.exercise: Calculate SINR and capacity across a cell layout under different reuse factors and sketch the 5G core control flow for a session set-up.

tasks.title: Compute SINR at the cell edge for reuse factors 1, 3 and 7 on a hexagonal layout and convert each to spectral efficiency
Model a 5G core with access and mobility, session and user plane functions and trace the messages for a session establishment
Compute the slot length, subcarrier spacing and resource grid size for several 5G numerologies and choose one for a latency target

schedule.title: Slicing, small cells and rural coverage
schedule.exercise: Design a rural fixed wireless service for ten villages, comparing macro-cell and small-cell options by cost per user.

tasks.title: Match six services to eMBB, URLLC or mMTC slices in a case and justify the required bandwidth, latency and reliability for each
Add small cells to a congested macro cell in the simulator and measure the change in user throughput and handover count
Compute the cost per subscriber of covering a district with towers of different heights and spectrum bands, and find the break-even take-up rate

schedule.title: MIMO, precoding and beamforming
schedule.exercise: Compare zero-forcing and MMSE precoding for a multi-user downlink and show channel hardening as the antenna count grows.

tasks.title: Compute the singular values of a 2 by 2 channel matrix and the capacity gain of spatial multiplexing over a single antenna
Simulate zero-forcing and MMSE precoding for four users and compare the sum rate at low and high SNR
Simulate massive MIMO with 16 to 256 antennas and pilot reuse, and show channel hardening and the sum-rate loss from pilot contamination

schedule.title: Mobility models and handover
schedule.exercise: Tune handover parameters for a rail corridor to minimise ping-pong and failure, using a mobility model and a two-cell simulator.

tasks.title: Move a user between two cells and record the signal levels at which handover triggers with three different hysteresis settings
Generate random waypoint and Gauss-Markov traces, measure the average handover rate for each, and explain the difference
Optimise hysteresis and time-to-trigger for a user at 120 km/h to keep handover failures below 1 percent with few ping-pong events

schedule.title: LPWAN and short-range IoT
schedule.exercise: Plan a LoRaWAN network for a farm with 500 soil sensors, checking duty cycle limits, spreading factors and battery life.

tasks.title: Compute the airtime, maximum message rate under a 1 percent duty cycle and receiver sensitivity for each LoRa spreading factor
Model a sensor node with sleep, listen and transmit states, and compute battery life for three duty cycle settings
Simulate 500 LoRa nodes with random access around one gateway and find the spreading factor assignment that maximises delivery ratio

schedule.title: Sensor routing, energy and localisation
schedule.exercise: Compare LEACH clustering with direct transmission for network lifetime and design an energy-harvesting node for a solar-powered sensor.

tasks.title: Locate a node by trilateration from three noisy range measurements and plot the position error as noise grows
Compare multi-hop routing with direct transmission in a sensor field and record when the first node dies in each
Size a solar panel and battery for a sensor node under a measured cloud-cover profile so it never runs out of energy over a year

schedule.title: Orbits, link budgets and LEO constellations
schedule.exercise: Compute a satellite downlink budget with rain fade and compare the latency of a geostationary link with a low-orbit constellation.

tasks.title: Compute the orbital period, altitude and round-trip delay for GEO, MEO and LEO satellites and compare the three
Complete a downlink budget with EIRP, path loss, rain fade and G/T, and find the link margin and the maximum data rate
Simulate a LEO pass over Accra, computing visibility windows, Doppler shift and handover times between two satellites

schedule.title: Satellite access, NTN and remote connectivity
schedule.exercise: Recommend satellite, terrestrial or hybrid backhaul for a remote island community, using capacity, latency and cost evidence.

tasks.title: Run a TCP transfer over a 600 ms delay link and observe how window size limits throughput, then raise the window to compensate
Compare coverage radius, capacity and latency of a high-altitude platform, a drone relay and a tower for a flood-affected district
Work a connectivity case for three remote communities, choosing technology and scoring the plan on cost, resilience and sustainability

schedule.title: Research methods and project
schedule.exercise: Reproduce one published wireless result by simulation, report it with confidence intervals, and present the project design for review.

tasks.title: Read a short testbed paper excerpt and answer questions on its measurements, assumptions and the limits of its conclusions
Run a fading channel simulation with enough trials to bound the BER estimate error and report the 95 percent confidence interval
Evaluate the project coverage or IoT design in the network simulator under peak load and a base station failure, and report the margins
